name: Circle USYC
oneLiner: Circle USYC is Circle's tokenized T-bill fund share backed by short-term U.S. Treasuries and reverse repos, redeemable at NAV.
collateral: Short-term U.S. Treasury bills and reverse repo agreements held for Circle USYC / Hashnote fund shares in segregated brokerage and custody accounts.
pegMechanism: Same-day subscription and redemption via USDC at NAV-based token price

applicabilityBasis.summary: USYC represents shares of the Hashnote International Short Duration Fund Ltd., a Cayman Islands mutual fund administered by Circle International Bermuda Limited. It is a yield-bearing tokenized fund share with NAV exposure rather than a fixed-value payment stablecoin, so it is treated as an excluded security for GENIUS tracking.

genius.issuerEntity: Circle International Bermuda Limited (token administrator, BMA-licensed); Hashnote International Short Duration Fund Ltd. (Cayman Islands mutual fund)
genius.notes: USYC is a tokenized fund share in the Hashnote International Short Duration Fund Ltd. (Cayman Islands registered mutual fund), not a payment stablecoin. The GENIUS Act payment-stablecoin framework does not apply: USYC is yield-bearing via NAV appreciation, not fixed-value, and represents a securities interest. Circle acquired Hashnote in January 2025; the token administrator is Circle International Bermuda Limited, regulated by the Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA) under its DABA License.

mintAuthority.summary: USYC issuance is issuer-controlled. On Ethereum and BSC the token owner() is an issuer EOA (MPC/HSM custody expected). On Solana the mint/freeze authority is a PDA of an unidentified BPFLoaderUpgradeable program owned by EMfvuBR8 — consistent with issuer-operated custodial minting.

review.evidence: Ethereum and BSC owner() confirmed as EOAs at blocks 25294716 and 103622902; eth_getCode returns 0x (no bytecode) on both. Solana mint authority is DZ7j2YL (issuer-controlled PDA of BPFLoaderUpgradeable program). EOA ownership on main chains is expected for enterprise MPC/HSM custody and corroborates the issuer-operated model; no permissionless mint route exists.
